painful_workflow: Intake coordinators must explain how one stale document, OCR error, or missing benefit letter changes application readiness while avoiding any approval, denial, rank, score, or eligibility conclusion.
current_workaround: Manual side-by-side packet reviews, informal what-if explanations, and resubmission checklists that lose the exact field change, source box, applicant correction, and non-decision boundary.
imported_mechanism: From m3: constraint-aware cohort anomaly detection becomes constraint-aware packet counterfactual detection. The system normalizes extracted document fields, applies one program-year rule constraints, detects impossible or stale values, and runs bounded counterfactual packet states such as corrected wage, fresh pay period, or added benefit letter while keeping original and changed fields separate.
core_computation: GPT-5.6 role: explains counterfactual packet differences in plain language, names which field changed, and labels every sentence as source-backed, calculated, or abstained while refusing eligibility conclusions. Codex role: implements the extraction fixture, constraint checker, counterfactual comparison engine, prompt-injection tests, WCAG-focused UI states, audit export, and verification harness tied to https://github.com/ElaineQian09/Hack_Nation_6th_Global_AI_Hackathon with evidence id src-3387c893a95d.
last_mile_action: Triggers a counterfactual comparison: the coordinator selects one applicant-approved correction or replacement document, and the app generates a before/after packet mirror showing changed requirements, unchanged requirements, abstentions, and the export-blocking reason without sending or deciding the application.
visible_transformation: Demo starts with a synthetic packet blocked by one stale pay period and one OCR wage anomaly; triggering the counterfactual comparison shows the original packet on the left, the corrected packet on the right, highlighted source boxes, and a readiness export button that becomes available only after applicant confirmation.
sponsor_dependency: GPT-5.6 reasoning and Codex-built evaluation harness
technical_risk: quality of the fixed evaluation fixture
why_now: The Databricks challenge supplies 10,000 Indian healthcare facility records with sparse capacity and doctor coverage fields, and its top judging weights emphasize evidence, trust, product judgment, and decision-support persistence.
killer_demo: Measurable before/after: before the counterfactual, the packet mirror shows 2 blocking issues, 3 abstained readiness sentences, and export disabled; after replacing the stale pay stub and correcting the OCR wage value, it shows 0 blocking issues, 1 remaining abstention, and a human-review export with the counterfactual diff attached. Five-day build plan: Day 1 define synthetic document fixture, one-year rule constraints, non-decision policy, and baseline checklist metric; Day 2 build field extraction with source boxes and original-value preservation; Day 3 implement constraint-aware anomaly detection plus counterfactual packet comparison; Day 4 build the side-by-side coordinator UI, applicant confirmation, deletion, and audit export; Day 5 benchmark against a manual checklist baseline and record the blocked-to-exportable packet mirror demo.
hard_to_fake_advantage: The hard part is preserving two auditable packet states with constraint explanations and non-decision guardrails. GPT-5.6 makes the differences understandable without crossing into eligibility advice, while Codex enforces deterministic rules, source-box traceability, deletion state, and regression tests for prompt-injection and accessibility.

gpt_5_6_role: GPT-5.6 performs the central constrained reasoning transformation and emits evidence-linked structured decisions
codex_build_role: Codex builds the executable prototype, test fixtures, evaluation harness, and records the required session
